name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Adopt a **hybrid triage system**: a pre-trained classifier flags obvious red flags (e.g., hate speech, copyright violations) *before* human review, while humans handle edge cases. This cuts review time by 40% without sacrificing accuracy—trade-off is upfront cost to train the classifier. Product owns the classifier; Legal owns the final ruleset.

name: Scriv
text: The hybrid triage system’s 40% time cut assumes the classifier’s public-contract blind spot is solved—it isn’t. Custom terms (e.g., brand-specific slurs) will slip through until the model is retrained, and that delay erodes trust faster than the speed gain. Instead, mandate a rolling 48-hour human audit of classifier outputs for the first 30 days; if false negatives exceed 5%, revert to 100% human review. Settle it with a live dashboard tracking classifier precision by category.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt a **24-hour rolling human triage** for edge cases flagged by the classifier, run by Legal with Product oversight. This closes the blind spot for custom terms and slurs faster than retraining the model, preserving trust without sacrificing the speed gains from automation. Trade-off: higher short-term labor cost, but it prevents downstream damage from missed violations.

name: Sift
text: The 24-hour rolling human triage still treats symptoms, not the root cause: custom terms and slurs will keep surfacing until the classifier’s training data is updated in real time. Instead, Legal and Product should co-own a live feedback loop where reviewers flag missed terms immediately, triggering model retraining within 6 hours—no human triage window needed. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with a shared dashboard tracking missed terms and retraining speed; if the model’s error rate drops below 2% within that window, the pilot wins.

name: Scope
text: Legal and Product co-own a live feedback loop: reviewers flag missed custom terms or slurs in real time, triggering immediate classifier retraining. This cuts blind spots faster than rolling triage or retraining cycles, preserving trust without sacrificing speed. Trade-off: higher short-term operational load for long-term accuracy and scalability.

name: Scriv
text: The live feedback loop assumes reviewers can spot every custom term in real time—miss one, and the blind spot widens. Instead, mandate a weekly classifier retraining cycle with Legal and Product jointly auditing the top 10 missed terms from the prior week; settle the argument by measuring the reduction in missed terms after two cycles.

name: Reel
text: Legal and Product jointly run a **weekly classifier retraining cycle**, auditing the top 10 missed custom terms or slurs from the prior week. This closes blind spots faster than real-time flagging—reviewers can’t catch everything in the moment—and avoids the operational drag of constant retraining. Trade-off: we accept a 24-hour lag for edge cases, but the data-driven fixes prevent trust erosion from repeated misses.

name: Scriv
text: The weekly retraining cycle ignores the fact that custom terms evolve faster than the audit can catch them—missed slurs in week 2 could poison the dataset before week 3’s retraining. Instead, mandate a **daily 15-minute Legal-Product huddle** to triage the classifier’s top 5 false negatives from the prior 24 hours, with the artifact being a shared log of resolved terms. Settle the argument by measuring the weekly volume of new custom terms caught versus the operational cost of the huddle.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt a **daily 15-minute Legal-Product huddle** to triage the classifier’s top 5 false negatives from the prior 24 hours. This catches evolving slurs and custom terms faster than weekly retraining while avoiding the overload of real-time flagging. Trade-off: it demands strict discipline to keep the huddle short and focused, but the speed gain in trust and accuracy outweighs the operational cost.

name: Sift
text: The daily huddle risks becoming a ritual that drains Legal and Product without solving the core problem: the classifier’s training data is stale by the time it’s updated. Instead, mandate that Legal and Engineering co-own a **live, auto-triggered retraining pipeline**—where any flagged false negative immediately queues a retraining job, but only deploys after a 24-hour Legal review to prevent poisoned data. Settle the argument by measuring the reduction in false negatives *and* the time-to-deploy for fixes over two weeks.

name: Scope
text: Adopt a **live, auto-triggered retraining pipeline** where Legal and Engineering co-own the trigger: any flagged false negative (missed slur or custom term) immediately queues a retraining run. This cuts blind spots faster than scheduled huddles or weekly cycles because it reacts to real usage, not calendar time. Trade-off: it demands strict discipline to keep the trigger clean—over-flagging risks training churn, under-flagging leaves gaps.

name: Scriv
text: The live, auto-triggered retraining pipeline risks drowning Engineering in ad-hoc workloads—every false negative becomes a fire drill, and the classifier’s stability suffers. Instead, mandate a **daily 15-minute Legal-Product huddle** to triage the top 5 false negatives, but with a hard cap: only terms that recur in ≥3 transcripts trigger immediate retraining; others queue for the weekly cycle. Settle it by measuring false negative reduction over 30 days—if the huddle misses >20% of high-impact terms, escalate to the pipeline.

name: Reel
text: Adopt a **hybrid triage system**: a pre-trained classifier flags obvious red flags in real time, while Legal and Product jointly run a **weekly classifier retraining cycle**, auditing the top 10 missed custom terms or slurs from the prior week. This keeps the system responsive to fast-moving slurs without overloading Engineering with ad-hoc retraining, trading immediate precision for sustainable discipline.

name: Scriv
text: The hybrid system still lets slurs slip through in real time—the pre-trained classifier’s red flags are only as good as the last retraining, and weekly audits won’t catch what’s already poisoned the dataset. Instead, mandate a **real-time, low-latency triage queue** where Legal flags the top 3 false negatives within 1 hour of detection, auto-triggering a micro-retraining run that Engineering must complete within 4 hours. That settles it: either the queue stays empty and the system works, or it fills and forces a fix—no rituals, no stale data.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt a **real-time, low-latency triage queue** where Legal flags the top 3 false negatives within 15 minutes of detection, triggering an immediate classifier update. This beats all other options because it balances speed and control—Legal’s real-time input fixes the most urgent slurs before they spread, while the queue prevents Engineering overload by capping updates to only the highest-impact cases. Trade-off: Legal must staff this queue 24/7, but it’s the only way to guarantee slurs don’t fester while avoiding the chaos of ad-hoc retraining.

name: Sift
text: The real-time queue risks flooding Engineering with low-signal noise—Legal may flag 3 false negatives per incident, but 80% are duplicates or noise. Instead, mandate a **daily 10-minute Legal-Engineering triage** on the top 5 *unique* false negatives, with a hard rule: only retrain if the classifier’s confidence in the batch drops below 85%. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with metrics on slur escape rate and Engineering load.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the **real-time, low-latency triage queue** where Legal flags the top 3 false negatives within 15 minutes, triggering an immediate classifier update. This balances speed and control—Legal’s real-time input fixes the most urgent slurs before they spread, while Engineering avoids drowning in ad-hoc noise by limiting retraining to high-signal cases. The trade-off is accepting occasional over-correction if Legal flags borderline terms, but that’s safer than letting slurs slip through in real time.

name: Scriv
text: The real-time queue will drown Legal in false alarms—15 minutes is too short for meaningful review, and "top 3" guarantees they’ll miss the patterns that matter. Instead, mandate a **daily 15-minute Legal-Product huddle** to triage the top 5 *unique* false negatives, with a hard cap: only retrain if the classifier’s confidence in the error exceeds 80%. That settles it: Legal controls the signal, Engineering avoids noise, and the artifact is the huddle’s triage log.

name: Reel
text: Adopt a **daily 15-minute Legal-Product huddle** to triage the top 5 *unique* false negatives, with a hard cap: only retrain if the classifier’s confidence in those terms drops below 60%. This keeps Legal focused on high-signal cases instead of drowning in noise, while Product ensures the retraining stays aligned with current slur patterns. The trade-off is accepting a slight delay (up to 24 hours) for the most urgent fixes, but it prevents wasted effort on duplicates and maintains a clean, actionable queue.

name: Scriv
text: The daily huddle ignores the real-time harm: slurs spread faster than a 15-minute batch can catch them. Worse, a 60% confidence cap lets borderline cases fester—Legal’s job is to block harm, not gamble on thresholds. **Settle it:** run a **real-time queue filtered by Legal’s "harm severity" rubric**, then batch the survivors into a daily 10-minute deep dive for retraining.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt a **real-time, low-latency triage queue** where Legal flags the top 3 *harm-severity* false negatives within 10 minutes, triggering an immediate classifier update. This beats all other options because it balances speed and control—Legal’s real-time input fixes the most urgent slurs before they spread, while Engineering avoids drowning in noise by trusting Legal’s harm rubric. The trade-off is accepting some false positives in the queue, but the harm prevented outweighs the noise.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s real-time queue risks burning Legal’s credibility—flagging only the "top 3" by harm severity guarantees they’ll miss the systemic patterns that create 80% of the noise. Instead, mandate a **daily 10-minute Legal-Engineering triage on the top 5 unique false negatives**, with a hard rule: only retrain if the classifier’s confidence in those terms drops below 70%. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with both models, measuring Legal’s false-positive load and slur spread time.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the **real-time, low-latency triage queue** where Legal flags the top 3 *harm-severity* false negatives within 10 minutes, triggering an immediate classifier update. name: Scriv

name: Reel

The trade-off is Legal’s time—this demands their constant availability—but the alternative is letting harm propagate unchecked.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s 5-minute Legal flag risks misclassifying harm—slurs evolve faster than human review, and "top 3" still ignores systemic patterns.
